defect.summary: At episode confirmation, the trough search ran from the frozen reference high through confirmation. A prior one-day >=2% dip that failed confirmation could therefore become the low of a later separately confirmed episode.
consequences: inflated no-new-low persistence and potentially early stabilization/recovery
defect.not_affected: The frozen episode peak/reference itself was correct and remains unchanged.

repair.rule: Episode low initialization is restricted to the current contiguous confirmation attempt: pending.first_index through confirmation inclusive.
repair.gap_safety: Pending confirmation resets across an unobserved expected session, so this interval cannot bridge a data gap.
repair.discriminator: 96.0 one-day dip (fails confirmation), recover to 100,100,100, then 97.0 -> 98.0. The later episode confirms at 98 with low=97, no-new-low=1, loss-recovered=33.33%; the old 96 dip is excluded.

frozen_lifecycle_contract.rolling_reference: exact trailing 63 settled closes including current
frozen_lifecycle_contract.stabilization: three observed sessions without a new low + close above five-close average
frozen_lifecycle_contract.recovery: five consecutive closes above rising 20-close average + ten observed sessions without new low
frozen_lifecycle_contract.trend_repair: 20 consecutive closes above the 20-close average + rising 20-close average + current above preceding 19 closes + at least 21 observed sessions without new low
frozen_lifecycle_contract.confirmation_rebound: when first pending close is the trough and second qualifying close confirms while rebounding, confirmation counts as first no-new-low session
frozen_lifecycle_contract.false_start_isolation: unconfirmed prior dip cannot seed the low/recovery clock of a later episode

initial_discriminator_test_error.result: test initially used 98.5 as the second close, which is only 1.5% below a 100 reference and correctly does not confirm; fixture corrected to exact qualifying 98.0 without weakening production thresholds
